newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovene NLB bank awarded an A- rating by BankWatch.
newsitem.headline: Slovene NLB bank awarded an A- rating by BankWatch.

text.p: Bank rating agency Thompson BankWatch-Bree said on Thursday it awarded a senior debt long-term rating of A- to Slovenia's largest bank state-owned Nova Ljubljanska Banka (NLB).

"The (NLB) senior debt rating is the highest Thomson BankWatch has assigned to any bank in Central and Eastern Europe and it reflects the state's full ownership of the bank as well as NLB's weight in the banking system," the agency said in a statement.
Previously BankWatch had no long-term rating for NLB.
The bank has a 27 percent market share in Slovenia's crowded banking sector that includes a total of 28 banks.
"Asset quality is good and liquidity is much improved... State bonds still generate a large proportion of interest income but profits are rising steadily," the agency said of the bank.
"NLB brought new products and services to the market while management worked to transform the bank into a more customer- oriented institution," it added.
